headline: High risk of cascading error and capability conflict: gpt-engineer can write/run code from prompts while godot_rl_agents is a game-playing repo with no isolation, so unsafe outputs can be turned into executed project changes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented between godot_rl_agents and gpt-engineer, so classic prompt injection is not evidenced. However, gpt-engineer writes files and then offers to run them, and its project-directory workflow can ingest user-provided content; if godot_rl_agents outputs are manually copied into that workspace, malicious instructions could ride along. The pathway is unusual and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF outputs from godot_rl_agents are manually pasted into gpt-engineer prompts or project files, THEN injected instructions can be reinterpreted as commands.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, THEN the injection pathway becomes direct.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not copy model output into executable files.
Review any pasted text for instruction-like content.
Disable any auto-run step in gpt-engineer.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: godot_rl_agents shows no data classes touched and no filesystem or network surfaces, while gpt-engineer reads and writes a user-specified project directory and can send prompts to a configured model. There is no documented shared workspace or sensitive-data flow from A to B, so leakage is not default; the main risk appears only if the operator places secrets into the shared project directory.
conditions: IF secrets or private source files are placed in gpt-engineer's project directory, THEN they may be sent to the configured model backend.
IF godot_rl_agents is extended to emit sensitive artifacts into the same directory, THEN B can read them.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the project directory.
Use a throwaway workspace for generated code.
Redact sensitive files before running gpt-engineer.
Verify model-provider logging settings.
requires-engineering: add directory-level secret scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer has write_filesystem, execute_shell, spawn_subprocesses, and per-project shared state via the project directory, while godot_rl_agents is a game-playing repo with no isolation or locking surface documented. If both are pointed at the same directory, B can overwrite or race with artifacts produced by A. The conflict is plausible in default project workflows, though not proven to be destructive by itself.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory, THEN writes can collide.
IF gpt-engineer executes generated shell commands, THEN it can mutate files created by the other agent.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Serialize access with a simple operator checklist.
Back up the project directory before runs.
Avoid running generated shell commands automatically.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer is designed to generate code from prompts and then offer to run it, so it can treat upstream text as authoritative. godot_rl_agents is a game/simulation repo that may produce outputs later consumed by B; if those outputs are accepted without verification, B can turn mistaken or adversarial content into executed code or project changes. The downstream action-taking authority makes the blast radius potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents outputs are used as specifications for gpt-engineer, THEN B may implement them without verification.
IF the operator approves execution of generated code, THEN erroneous upstream content can become live changes.
mitigations: Require human review before execution.
Compare outputs against a trusted spec.
Run generated code in a disposable sandbox.
Keep A's outputs as advisory only.
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for godot_rl_agents, while gpt-engineer handles generated source code and may send prompts to a configured model. Because only B has a documented external model call surface, compliance risk is limited to whatever data the operator places into B; A is not cited for a separate compliance regime. The other agent is not cited because no distinct compliance constraint is documented for it.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into gpt-engineer's prompts or project files, THEN it may flow to an external model provider.
IF the operator requires a residency or retention guarantee that the configured model lacks, THEN compliance may be breached.
mitigations: Do not input regulated data.
Use a compliant model endpoint.
Review retention settings before use.
Keep generated code free of personal data.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data filtering.
